problem_description.description: The leader of some very secretive organization has decided to invite all other members to a meeting. All members of the organization live in the same town which can be represented as $$$n$$$ crossroads connected by $$$m$$$ two-directional streets. The meeting will be held in the leader's house near the crossroad $$$1$$$. There are $$$k$$$ members of the organization invited to the meeting; $$$i$$$-th of them lives near the crossroad $$$a_i$$$. All members of the organization receive the message about the meeting at the same moment and start moving to the location where the meeting is held. In the beginning of each minute each person is located at some crossroad. He or she can either wait a minute at this crossroad, or spend a minute to walk from the current crossroad along some street to another crossroad (obviously, it is possible to start walking along the street only if it begins or ends at the current crossroad). In the beginning of the first minute each person is at the crossroad where he or she lives. As soon as a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, he or she immediately comes to the leader's house and attends the meeting.Obviously, the leader wants all other members of the organization to come up as early as possible. But, since the organization is very secretive, the leader does not want to attract much attention. Let's denote the discontent of the leader as follows  initially the discontent is $$$0$$$;  whenever a person reaches the crossroad number $$$1$$$, the discontent of the leader increases by $$$c \cdot x$$$, where $$$c$$$ is some fixed constant, and $$$x$$$ is the number of minutes it took the person to reach the crossroad number $$$1$$$;  whenever $$$x$$$ members of the organization walk along the same street at the same moment in the same direction, $$$dx^2$$$ is added to the discontent, where $$$d$$$ is some fixed constant. This is not cumulative: for example, if two persons are walking along the same street in the same direction at the same moment, then $$$4d$$$ is added to the discontent, not $$$5d$$$. Before sending a message about the meeting, the leader can tell each member of the organization which path they should choose and where they should wait. Help the leader to establish a plan for every member of the organization so they all reach the crossroad $$$1$$$, and the discontent is minimized.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains five integer numbers $$$n$$$, $$$m$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 50$$$, $$$n - 1 \le m \le 50$$$, $$$1 \le k, c, d \le 50$$$) — the number of crossroads, the number of streets, the number of persons invited to the meeting and the constants affecting the discontent, respectively. The second line contains $$$k$$$ numbers $$$a_1$$$, $$$a_2$$$, ..., $$$a_k$$$ ($$$2 \le a_i \le n$$$) — the crossroads where the members of the organization live. Then $$$m$$$ lines follow, each denoting a bidirectional street. Each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$, $$$x_i \ne y_i$$$) denoting a street connecting crossroads $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. There may be multiple streets connecting the same pair of crossroads. It is guaranteed that every crossroad can be reached from every other crossroad using the given streets.
problem_description.output_spec: Print one integer: the minimum discontent of the leader after everyone reaches crossroad $$$1$$$.
problem_description.notes: NoteThe best course of action in the first test is the following:  the first person goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the second person waits one minute on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the third person waits two minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting;  the fourth person waits three minutes on the crossroad $$$3$$$, then goes along the street $$$2$$$ to the crossroad $$$2$$$, then goes along the street $$$1$$$ to the crossroad $$$1$$$ and attends the meeting.

import sys
from collections import deque

N = 10000
M = N * 100
inf = 1 << 60

class FlowGraph:
    def __init__(self):
        self.head = [-1] * N
        self.v = [0] * M
        self.nxt = [-1] * M
        self.c = [0] * M
        self.w = [0] * M
        self.ptr = 0
        self.cost = 0
        self.t = 0

        self.dis = [-1] * N
        self.id = [0] * N
        self.cur = [-1] * N
        self.vis = [False] * N

    def padd_edge(self, uu, vv, ww, cc):
        self.v[self.ptr] = vv
        self.w[self.ptr] = ww
        self.c[self.ptr] = cc
        self.nxt[self.ptr] = self.head[uu]
        self.head[uu] = self.ptr
        self.ptr += 1

    def add_edge(self, u, v, w, c):
        self.padd_edge(u, v, w, c)
        self.padd_edge(v, u, 0, -c)

    def spfa(self, s, t):
        for i in range(len(self.vis)):
            self.vis[i] = False
            self.dis[i] = -1
        q = deque()
        q.append(s)
        self.dis[s] = 0
        self.id[s] = 1
        while q:
            nd = q.popleft()
            self.vis[nd] = False
            i = self.head[nd]
            while i != -1:
                if self.w[i] and (self.dis[self.v[i]] == -1 or self.dis[self.v[i]] > self.dis[nd] + self.c[i]):
                    self.dis[self.v[i]] = self.dis[nd] + self.c[i]
                    if not self.vis[self.v[i]]:
                        self.vis[self.v[i]] = True
                        q.append(self.v[i])
                i = self.nxt[i]
        return self.dis[t] != -1

    def dfs(self, pos, flow, t):
        if pos == t:
            return flow
        self.vis[pos] = True
        tmp = flow
        i = self.cur[pos]
        if i == -1:
            i = self.head[pos]
        while i != -1:
            if (not self.vis[self.v[i]] and self.w[i] and self.dis[self.v[i]] == self.dis[pos] + self.c[i]):
                self.cur[pos] = i
                fl = self.dfs(self.v[i], min(flow, self.w[i]), t)
                self.cost += fl * self.c[i]
                self.w[i] -= fl
                self.w[i ^ 1] += fl
                flow -= fl
                if flow == 0:
                    break
            i = self.nxt[i]
        self.vis[pos] = False
        return tmp - flow

    def dinic(self, s, t):
        self.cost = 0
        self.t = t
        while self.spfa(s, t):
            for i in range(len(self.cur)):
                self.cur[i] = self.head[i]
            self.dfs(s, inf, t)
        return self.cost

import sys
from collections import deque

def add(u, v, flow, cost):
    to.append(v)
    ct.append(cost)
    w.append(flow)
    nt.append(head[u])
    head[u] = len(to) - 1
    
    to.append(u)

def init():
    global head, to, ct, w, nt, tot
    head = [-1] * (N + 1)
    to = []
    ct = []
    w = []
    nt = []
    tot = 0

def spfa(s, t):
    d = [float('inf')] * (N + 1)
    vis = [False] * (N + 1)
    pre = [-1] * (N + 1)
    id = [-1] * (N + 1)
    d[s] = 0
    q = deque([s])
    while q:
        u = q.popleft()
        for i in range(head[u], -1, -1):
            i = head[u]
            while i != -1:
                if w[i] > 0 and d[to[i]] > d[u] + ct[i]:
                    d[to[i]] = d[u] + ct[i]
                    pre[to[i]] = u
                    id[to[i]] = i
                    if not vis[to[i]]:
                        vis[to[i]] = True
                        q.append(to[i])
                i = nt[i]
        vis[u] = False
    return d, pre, id, d[t] < float('inf')

def MaxFlow(s, t):
    total = 0
    total_cost = 0
    while True:
        d, pre, id, path_exists = spfa(s, t)
        if not path_exists:
            break
        Mi = float('inf')
        i = t
        while i != s:
            Mi = min(Mi, w[id[i]])
            i = pre[i]
        i = t
        while i != s:
            w[id[i]] -= Mi
            w[id[i] ^ 1] += Mi
            i = pre[i]
        total += Mi
        total_cost += d[t] * Mi
    return total_cost

e = []

def add_edge(u, v, cap, cost):
    e.append([u, v, cap, 0, cost])
    g[u].append(len(e) - 1)
    e.append([v, u, 0, 0, -cost])
    g[v].append(len(e) - 1)

dist = [INF] * MAXN
pre = [-1] * MAXN
cap = [0] * MAXN
inq = [False] * MAXN

def flow(s, t):
    total_flow = 0
    total_cost = 0
    while True:
        for i in range(len(dist)):
            dist[i] = INF
        dist[s] = 0
        for i in range(len(pre)):
            pre[i] = -1
        pre[s] = 0
        for i in range(len(cap)):
            cap[i] = 0
        cap[s] = INF
        for i in range(len(inq)):
            inq[i] = False
        from collections import deque
        q = deque()
        q.append(s)
        inq[s] = True
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            inq[u] = False
            for it in g[u]:
                f = e[it]
                if f[2] - f[3] > 1e-9 and dist[f[1]] > dist[u] + f[4] + 1e-9:
                    dist[f[1]] = dist[u] + f[4]
                    pre[f[1]] = it
                    cap[f[1]] = min(cap[u], f[2] - f[3])
                    if not inq[f[1]]:
                        q.append(f[1])
                        inq[f[1]] = True
        if pre[t] < 0:
            break
        total_flow += cap[t]
        total_cost += cap[t] * dist[t]
        v = t
        while v != s:
            e[pre[v]][3] += cap[t]
            e[pre[v]^1][3] -= cap[t]
            v = e[pre[v]][0]

class MinCostFlow:
    class Edge:
        def __init__(self, v, c, w, r):
            self.v = v
            self.c = c
            self.w = w
            self.r = r

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.G = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def add(self, u, v, c, w):
        j = len(self.G[v])
        i = len(self.G[u])
        self.G[u].append(self.Edge(v, c, w, j))
        self.G[v].append(self.Edge(u, 0, -w, i))

    def run(self, s, t, f):
        N = len(self.G)
        res = 0
        H = [0] * N
        D = [float('inf')] * N
        INF = 10**18
        PE = [0] * N
        PV = [0] * N
        while f > 0:
            q = []
            D = [float('inf')] * N
            D[s] = 0
            heapq.heappush(q, (0, s))
            while q:
                d, u = heapq.heappop(q)
                d = -d
                if D[u] < d:
                    continue
                for i, e in enumerate(self.G[u]):
                    if e.c > 0 and D[e.v] > D[u] + e.w + H[u] - H[e.v]:
                        D[e.v] = D[u] + e.w + H[u] - H[e.v]
                        heapq.heappush(q, (-D[e.v], e.v))
                        PV[e.v] = u
                        PE[e.v] = i
            if D[t] == float('inf'):
                return -1
            for i in range(N):
                H[i] += D[i]
            d = f
            i = t
            while i != s:
                u = PV[i]
                e = self.G[u][PE[i]]
                d = min(d, e.c)
                i = u
            f -= d
            res += d * H[t]
            i = t
            while i != s:
                u = PV[i]
                e = self.G[u][PE[i]]
                e.c -= d
                self.G[i][e.r].c += d
                i = u
        return res

from collections import deque

class MCMF:
    def __init__(self, N=30000, M=7010010):
        self.N = N
        self.M = M
        self.h = [-1] * self.N
        self.ing = [0] * self.N
        self.pre = [0] * self.N
        self.to = [0] * self.M
        self.ne = [0] * self.M
        self.cap = [0] * self.M
        self.dis = [float('inf')] * self.N
        self.cost = [0] * self.M
        self.e = 0
        self.s = 0
        self.t = 0
        self.n = 0

    def ini(self, _n):
        self.h = [-1] * _n
        self.n = _n
        self.e = 0

    def liu(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.to[self.e] = v
        self.ne[self.e] = self.h[u]
        self.cap[self.e] = c
        self.cost[self.e] = w
        self.h[u] = self.e
        self.e += 1

    def link(self, u, v, c, w):
        self.liu(u, v, c, w)
        self.liu(v, u, 0, -w)

    def spfa(self):
        for i in range(self.n):
            self.dis[i] = float('inf')
            self.ing[i] = 0
        Q = deque()
        Q.append(self.s)
        self.dis[self.s] = 0
        self.ing[self.s] = 1
        while Q:
            c = Q.popleft()
            self.ing[c] = 0
            k = self.h[c]
            while k != -1:
                v = self.to[k]
                if self.cap[k] > 0 and self.dis[c] + self.cost[k] < self.dis[v]:
                    self.dis[v] = self.dis[c] + self.cost[k]
                    self.pre[v] = k
                    if not self.ing[v]:
                        Q.append(v)
                        self.ing[v] = 1
                k = self.ne[k]
        return self.dis[self.t] != float('inf')

    def run(self, _s, _t):
        self.s = _s
        self.t = _t
        flow = 0
        mincost = 0
        while self.spfa():
            pl = float('inf')
            p = self.t
            while p != self.s:
                k = self.pre[p]
                pl = min(pl, self.cap[k])
                p = self.to[k ^ 1]
            p = self.t
            while p != self.s:
                k = self.pre[p]
                self.cap[k] -= pl
                self.cap[k ^ 1] += pl
                p = self.to[k ^ 1]
            mincost += pl * self.dis[self.t]
            flow += pl
        return flow, mincost

        self.G = []

        self.G = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def add_edge(self, fr, to, cap, cost):
        self.G[fr].append(Edge(to, cap, cost, len(self.G[to])))
        self.G[to].append(Edge(fr, 0, -cost, len(self.G[fr]) - 1))

    def minCost(self, s, t, f):
        import heapq
        flow = 0
        res = 0
        H = [0] * self.V
        while f > 0:
            dis = [float('inf')] * self.V
            dis[s] = 0
            pq = [(0, s)]
            PreV = [-1] * self.V
            PreE = [-1] * self.V
            while pq:
                cd, v = heapq.heappop(pq)
                if dis[v] < cd:
                    continue
                for i, e in enumerate(self.G[v]):
                    if e.capacity > 0 and dis[e.to] > dis[v] + e.cost + H[v] - H[e.to]:
                        dis[e.to] = dis[v] + e.cost + H[v] - H[e.to]
                        PreV[e.to] = v
                        PreE[e.to] = i
                        heapq.heappush(pq, (dis[e.to], e.to))
            if dis[t] == float('inf'):
                break
            for i in range(self.V):
                if dis[i] < float('inf'):
                    H[i] += dis[i]
            d = f
            v = t
            while v != s:
                u = PreV[v]
                e = self.G[u][PreE[v]]
                d = min(d, e.capacity)
                v = u
            f -= d
            flow += d
            res += d * H[t]
            v = t
            while v != s:
                u = PreV[v]
                e = self.G[u][PreE[v]]
                e.capacity -= d
                self.G[v][e.rev].capacity += d
                v = u
        return res

        self.G[u].append(m - 2)
        self.G[v].append(m - 1)

    def BelmanFord(self, flow, cost):
        for i in range(self.n):
            self.d[i] = INF
        self.inq = [False]*self.n
        self.d[self.s] = 0
        self.inq[self.s] = True
        self.p[self.s] = 0
        self.a[self.s] = INF
        from collections import deque
        Q = deque([self.s])
        while Q:
            u = Q.popleft()
            self.inq[u] = False
            for i in self.G[u]:
                e = self.E[i]
                if e.cap > e.flow and self.d[e.v] > self.d[u] + e.cost:
                    self.d[e.v] = self.d[u] + e.cost
                    self.p[e.v] = i
                    self.a[e.v] = min(self.a[u], e.cap - e.flow)
                    if not self.inq[e.v]:
                        Q.append(e.v)
                        self.inq[e.v] = True
        if self.d[self.t] == INF:
            return False
        flow[0] = self.a[self.t]
        cost[0] = self.d[self.t]
        u = self.t
        while u != self.s:
            self.E[self.p[u]].flow += flow[0]
            self.E[self.p[u]^1].flow -= flow[0]
            u = self.E[self.p[u]].u
        return True

    def Mincost(self, s, t):
        self.s = s
        self.t = t
        totalFlow = 0
        totalCost = 0
        flow = [0]
        cost = [0]
        while self.BelmanFord(flow, cost):
            totalFlow += flow[0]
            totalCost += flow[0] * cost[0]
        return totalFlow, totalCost

def edmonds_karp(n, source, sink):
    flow = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    cap = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    pre = [-1]*n
    d = [0]*n
    INF = 0x3f3f3f3f

    total_flow = 0
    while True:
        for i in range(n):
            pre[i] = -1
        d[source] = INF
        queue = [source]
        p = 0
        q = 1
        while p < q and pre[sink] < 0:
            t = queue[p]
            p += 1
            for i in range(n):
                if pre[i] < 0 and cap[t][i] - flow[t][i] > 0:
                    pre[i] = t
                    d[i] = min(d[t], cap[t][i] - flow[t][i])
                    queue.append(i)
                    q += 1
        if pre[sink] < 0:
            break
        v = sink
        while v != source:
            u = pre[v]
            flow[u][v] += d[sink]
            flow[v][u] -= d[sink]
            v = u
        total_flow += d[sink]
        for i in range(n):
            pass
    return total_flow

    INF = 0x3f3f3f3f
    dir = [[0,1],[0,-1],[1,0],[-1,0]]
    mat = [[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            mat[i][j] = INF
    bi, bj = 0, 0

        while queue:
            now_i, now_j = queue.popleft()
            p_idx = now_i * n + now_j
            dis = vis[p_idx]
            if check:

                        vis[p_idx] = INF + 1
                    continue
            for d in range(4):

# Node and Edge declaration
class Node:
    def __init__(self):
        self.age = 0
        self.adjusted: List['Edge'] = []
        self.back: Optional['Edge'] = None

class Edge:
    def __init__(self):
        self.from_node: Optional[Node] = None
        self.to_node: Optional[Node] = None
        self.flow = 0
        self.opposite: Optional['Edge'] = None

def adjust(e: Optional['Edge'], d: int) -> int:
    if e is None:
        return d
    d = adjust(e.from_node.back, min(d, e.flow))
    e.flow -= d
    e.opposite.flow += d
    return d

def connect(a: Node, b: Node, w: int):
    ea = Edge()
    eb = Edge()
    ea.from_node = a
    ea.to_node = b
    ea.flow = w
    eb.from_node = b
    eb.to_node = a
    eb.flow = 0
    ea.opposite = eb
    eb.opposite = ea
    a.adjusted.append(ea)
    b.adjusted.append(eb)

def max_flow(g: List[Node], source: Node, sink: Node) -> int:
    result = 0
    while True:
        for u in g:
            u.age = 0
        q = deque()
        q.append(source)
        source.age = 1
        while q and sink.age == 0:
            u = q.popleft()
            for e in u.adjusted:
                v = e.to_node
                if v.age != 0 or e.flow == 0:
                    continue
                v.back = e
                v.age = u.age + 1
                q.append(v)
        if sink.age == 0:
            break
        for e in sink.adjusted:
            o = e.opposite
            if o.from_node.age != sink.age - 1 or o.flow == 0:
                continue
            result += adjust(o, o.flow)
    return result

    return t * n * n + r * n + c

problem_description.description: This is an easier version of the problem. In this version, $$$n \le 6$$$.Marek is working hard on creating strong testcases to his new algorithmic problem. You want to know what it is? Nah, we're not telling you. However, we can tell you how he generates the testcases.Marek chooses an integer $$$n$$$ and $$$n^2$$$ integers $$$p_{ij}$$$ ($$$1 \le i \le n$$$, $$$1 \le j \le n$$$). He then generates a random bipartite graph with $$$2n$$$ vertices. There are $$$n$$$ vertices on the left side: $$$\ell_1, \ell_2, \dots, \ell_n$$$, and $$$n$$$ vertices on the right side: $$$r_1, r_2, \dots, r_n$$$. For each $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$, he puts an edge between vertices $$$\ell_i$$$ and $$$r_j$$$ with probability $$$p_{ij}$$$ percent.It turns out that the tests will be strong only if a perfect matching exists in the generated graph. What is the probability that this will occur?It can be shown that this value can be represented as $$$\frac{P}{Q}$$$ where $$$P$$$ and $$$Q$$$ are coprime integers and $$$Q \not\equiv 0 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Let $$$Q^{-1}$$$ be an integer for which $$$Q \cdot Q^{-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{10^9+7}$$$. Print the value of $$$P \cdot Q^{-1}$$$ modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
problem_description.input_spec: The first line of the input contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$\mathbf{1 \le n \le 6}$$$). The following $$$n$$$ lines describe the probabilities of each edge appearing in the graph. maxN = 7
max2N = 1 << maxN
maxM = 100
maxS = 64184

sizes = [0, 5, 11, 37, 137, 821, 7529, 164184]
# Precalculate powers of 2 for n up to 6
def powmod(a, b):
    res = 1
    a %= MOD
    while b > 0:
        if b & 1:
            res = (res * a) % MOD
        a = (a * a) % MOD
        b >>= 1
    return res

# bit mask function
def bit(n):
    return 1 << n

# Represent a 128-bit bitset as an integer in Python
def bitu128(n):
    return 1 << n

# Read input data
tokens = input().split()
n = int(tokens[0])
m = n
pos = 1

# These arrays are used in the simulation

ind = [0] * maxS
bfs = [0] * maxS
match = [0] * maxS
next_mask = [[0]*maxS for _ in range(max2N)]  # size max2N x maxS
# Use dictionaries for adjacency to avoid large sparse arrays
# but here, since sizes are known, we'll initialize as list only if needed

# For the "precalc" procedure
def precalc(n):
    N = bit(n)

    fixed_size = [0] * (n+1)
    for mask in range(N):
        cnt = bin(mask).count('1')
        fixed_size[cnt] |= bitu128(mask)

    # Initialize hash table
    SZ = sizes[n]
    for i in range(SZ):
        what[i] = 0
    global len_bfs
    len_bfs = 0

    def get_ind(state):
        # Hash based on state bits
        # Since Python integers are unbounded, simulate modulo
        pos = 0
        for i in range(128):
            if (state >> i) & 1:
                pos = (pos * 2 + 1) % SZ
            else:
                pos = (pos * 2 + 0) % SZ
        start_pos = pos
        while True:
            if what[pos] == state:
                return ind[pos]
            if what[pos] == 0:
                what[pos] = state
                bfs[len_bfs] = state
                ind[pos] = len_bfs
                len_bfs += 1
                return ind[pos]
            pos = (pos + 1) % SZ
            if pos == start_pos:
                # Should not happen if hash table is sufficiently large
                raise RuntimeError("Hash table is full!")

    # Initialize BFS with empty graph (state=1)
    get_ind(1)

    for k in range(len_bfs):
        state = bfs[k]

        pred_hall = [0] * n
        for mask in range(N):
            if ((state >> mask) & 1) != 0:
                for i in range(n):
                    pred_hall[i] |= bitu128(mask | bit(i))
        for mask in range(N):
            nxt = state
            for i in range(n):
                if (mask & (1 << i)) != 0:
                    nxt |= pred_hall[i]
            next_mask[mask][k] = get_ind(nxt)

        for i in reversed(range(n+1)):
            if ((state & fixed_size[i]) != 0):
                match[k] = i
                break

for i in range(n):
    for j in range(m):
        val = int(tokens[pos])
        pos += 1
        p[i][j] = val * powmod(100, MOD - 2) % MOD

# Precompute states

prev = [0] * (length)
cur = [0] * (length)

prev[0] = 1

# Main computation
for j in range(m):
    for k in range(length):
        cur[k] = 0
    for mask in range(1 << n):
        prob = 1
        for i in range(n):
            if (mask & (1 << i)) != 0:
                prob = (prob * p[i][j]) % MOD
            else:
                prob = (prob * (MOD + 1 - p[i][j])) % MOD
        for k in range(length):
            cur[next_mask[mask][k]] = (cur[next_mask[mask][k]] + prob * prev[k]) % MOD
    prev, cur = cur, prev

# Calculate answer
ans = 0
for k in range(length):
    if match[k] == n:
        ans = (ans + prev[k]) % MOD

print(ans)

        self.h = n_

The shells are left on so there is no way to distinguish a raw egg from a cooked egg. One at a time, a player will select an egg, and then smash the egg on his/her forehead. If the egg was cooked, not much happens, but if the egg was raw, it will make quite the mess. This continues until one player has broken R raw eggs, at which point that player is declared the loser and the other player wins.The order in which players take turns can be described as a string of 'A' and 'B' characters, where the i-th character tells which player should choose the i-th egg. Traditionally, players take turns going one after the other. That is, they follow the ordering "ABABAB...". This isn't very fair though, because the second player will win more often than the first. We'd like you to find a better ordering for the players to take their turns. Let's define the unfairness of an ordering as the absolute difference between the first player's win probability and the second player's win probability. We're interested in orderings that minimize the unfairness. We only consider an ordering valid if it contains the same number of 'A's as 'B's.You will also be given a string S of length 2(R + C) containing only 'A', 'B', and '?' characters. An ordering is said to match S if it only differs from S in positions where S contains a '?'. Of the valid orderings that minimize unfairness, how many match S?

        if j == 0:
            C[i][j] = 1
        elif i == 0:
            C[i][j] = 0
        else:
            C[i][j] = C[i-1][j] + C[i-1][j-1]

total = C[r + c][r] * C[r + c][r]
best = 10**18
best_z = -1

# Function for DFS to compute minimal difference
def dfs(x, y, v1, v2):
    global best, best_z
    diff = abs(x - y)
    if best <= 1 or (diff - C[v1][r] * C[v2][r]) >= best:
        return
    if v1 == r - 1 and v2 == r - 1:
        diff = abs(x - y)
        if diff < best:
            best = diff
            best_z = x
        return
    if v1 >= r:
        cur1 = C[v1][r] - C[v1 - 1][r]
        sum2 = C[v2][r]
        dfs(x, y + cur1 * sum2, v1 - 1, v2)
    if v2 >= r:
        sum1 = C[v1][r]
        cur2 = C[v2][r] - C[v2 - 1][r]
        dfs(x + sum1 * cur2, y, v1, v2 - 1)

    else:

best = abs(x - y)

    res = 0
